Travelling with little ones in your campervan? Don't guess when it comes to safety.

Our M1 Certified U-Shape Seating Frame is the only M1-certified U-shape frame on the market — and it's built with families in mind. Every frame includes integrated ISOFIX anchor points and 3-point seatbelts, so you can fit a compatible child seat with confidence.

What does M1 certified actually mean? It means the frame has been independently crash-tested to ECE R14.09 — the same standard applied to seats in passenger cars. Without certification, rear seating in a campervan isn't legally compliant for carrying passengers in many circumstances.

Available in Standard (£1,999) and Full Width (£2,099). Compatible with VW T5, T6, T6.1 and Ford Transit Custom.

Most people assume all campervan seating is road-legal. It isn't.

Here's what the rules actually say:

🔹 Rear campervan seating is only legal for passenger use if the seat frame has been independently tested and certified to M1 standard (ECE R14.09).

🔹 ISOFIX in a campervan is only valid if the anchor points are part of an M1-certified installation — not just bolted to a plywood floor.

🔹 3-point seatbelts must be fitted for every seat position used while the vehicle is moving.

Most conversion furniture — even premium, expensive options — doesn't meet these requirements, because independent crash testing is costly and technically demanding.

If you're converting a van for family use, ask your supplier directly: 'Is this M1 certified?' If the answer is vague, that tells you what you need to know.

The school holidays are closer than they look. 🚐

There's something genuinely special about loading up the van with the kids and heading somewhere without a fixed itinerary. No hotel check-in times. No restaurant bookings. Just the freedom to stop when you want, explore what you find, and sleep wherever the day takes you.

A lot of parents tell us the campervan conversion was one of the best decisions they made — not just for weekend getaways, but for those longer summer trips where flexibility beats the cost and hassle of hotels.

The key is getting the setup right. A van that's safe, comfortable, and genuinely practical for family use is a very different thing from a solo weekend build — and it's absolutely achievable with the right foundation.
